title: B2+ · L21 — Idioms: emotions
description: Idioms sobre emociones: on cloud nine, down in the dumps, over the moon, y otros expresivos.

questions.prompt: Tu amiga acaba de conseguir el ascenso que llevaba anos persiguiendo.
questions.question: 'She's on cloud nine after the promotion' means:
options: She's currently sitting on an airplane.
She's feeling extremely happy and euphoric.
She's disappointed with the outcome.
She's confused about what happened.
questions.explanation: 'On cloud nine' = eufeorico, en la nube (feliz al maximo). Origen mitologico-meteorologico: en clasificacion de nubes de siglo XIX, la nueve era la cumulus mas alta. Uso tipico en momentos de gran alegria: promociones, weddings, victorias, embarazo esperado. Registro: neutro-conversacional. Colocacion fija: siempre 'ON cloud nine', nunca 'in' o 'at'. Error hispano: literal 'nube nueve' — no funciona, hay que usar 'en las nubes' o similar.
examples: I've been on cloud nine since the offer came through — I still can't quite believe it. → euforia post-oferta
She was on cloud nine after landing her dream job at the agency she'd stalked for years. → sueno cumplido

questions.prompt: Un colega no ha sonreido en toda la semana y su rendimiento ha bajado.
questions.question: 'He's been down in the dumps lately' means:
options: He's been physically inside a garbage dump.
He's been depressed or in a low mood.
He's been unusually happy and energetic.
He's been openly angry and aggressive.
questions.explanation: 'Down in the dumps' = deprimido, con animo bajo. 'Dumps' aqui es plural fosilizado, forma del ingles medio que sobrevivio solo en este idiom (nada que ver con vertederos). Registro: coloquial, neutro. Uso conversacional para describir estados temporales de tristeza, no depresion clinica seria. Alternativas: 'feeling low', 'in a funk', 'blue'. Error hispano cultural: en anglo se habla de estados emocionales mas abiertamente en small talk que en muchas culturas hispanas.
examples: She's been down in the dumps since the breakup — give her some time. → apoyo emocional
Don't stay down in the dumps too long — call your friends and get out. → consejo casual

questions.statement: 'To be over the moon' means to be delighted or ecstatic.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Over the moon' = eufeorico, extremadamente feliz. Origen britanico (rima infantil 'Hey Diddle Diddle' del siglo XVIII: la vaca salta por encima de la luna). Registro tipicamente britanico, aunque usado en anglo global. Sinonimo funcional de 'on cloud nine' y 'thrilled'. Colocacion fija: 'over the moon ABOUT' (nunca 'for'). Uso comun en anuncios de bodas, embarazos, aceptaciones academicas.
examples: I'm absolutely over the moon about the baby news — we've been trying for years. → alegria intima
She was over the moon when she heard she got into Oxford. → aceptacion academica

questions.prompt: Tu padre acaba de leer un email del banco con un cargo inesperado de 800 euros.
questions.question: 'He blew a fuse when he heard the news' means:
options: He broke an electrical appliance.
He lost his temper and became very angry.
He successfully fixed a problem.
He was pleasantly surprised.
questions.explanation: 'Blow a fuse' = perder los estribos, estallar en enfado. Metafora electrica clara (fusible sobrecargado). Registro: neutro-informal, muy comun en narrativa de conflicto. Sinonimos escalonados: 'lose it' (informal), 'blow up' (comun), 'flip out' (mas dramatico), 'go ballistic' (extremo). Error hispano: confundir con 'blow it' (cagarla) — sonido similar, significados totalmente distintos. Colocacion: siempre 'blow A fuse' (con articulo).
examples: My dad blew a fuse when he saw my grades — I've never seen him that mad. → drama familiar
Don't blow a fuse over one bad review — let's talk about it calmly tomorrow. → consejo de calma

questions.text: I've been on edge all week — this project has me completely stressed out.
questions.explanation: Frase de confesion emocional casual. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'on edge' con enlazado /ɒnedʒ/, la /n/ y la /e/ se funden sin pausa. 'Stressed out' con doble consonante /st/ + /aʊt/, tiende a /strestaʊt/ con elision de la /d/. Colocaciones: 'on edge' (nervioso, tenso, hipersensible), 'stressed out' (agobiado — mas coloquial que 'stressed' seco). Error hispano: 'stressed' sin 'out' suena mas formal-clinico; en spoken casual se dice casi siempre 'stressed out'.
examples: She's on edge because of the audit next week — everyone's tiptoeing around her. → tension en oficina
I've been so stressed out I can't sleep properly — need a real break. → burnout personal

questions.prompt: Recibes la llamada de que aprobaste el examen final del que dependia todo tu ano.
questions.question: 'That took a weight off my shoulders' means:
options: That involved physical lifting.
That brought great relief from a burden.
That added a new burden to carry.
That caused a shoulder injury.
questions.explanation: 'Take a weight off my shoulders' = aliviar una preocupacion acumulada. Metafora universal (peso fisico = carga mental). Se dice tras noticias buenas que resuelven preocupaciones pendientes: examenes aprobados, deuda saldada, conflicto resuelto. Alternativa mas corta: 'a load off' o 'what a relief'. Colocacion fija: siempre 'weight OFF' (con 'off', no 'from'). Registro: neutro-conversacional.
examples: Passing the driving exam took such a weight off my shoulders — third attempt lucky. → alivio personal
Just talking about it took a weight off — I hadn't realised how much I was carrying. → catarsis emocional

questions.prompt: Empareja cada emotion idiom con su significado en espanol:
questions.explanation: Set emocional completo cubriendo espectro alegria-desesperacion. 'At (my/one's) wit's end' = agotamiento mental, no saber que mas hacer (colocacion tipica: 'I'm at my wit's end with...' + situacion frustrante). 'In high spirits' es la forma mas formal-elegante para 'de buen humor'; contraste con 'in low spirits' (poco usado hoy). 'On cloud nine' es US; 'over the moon' es UK — significan lo mismo pero registro geografico distinto.
examples: I'm at my wit's end with these delays — three months and still no answer from the supplier. → frustracion laboral
The team was in high spirits after closing the biggest deal of the year. → animo colectivo

questions.target: I was on cloud nine after the offer came in, but the next morning I woke up feeling weirdly on edge about it.
questions.explanation: Contraste emocional realista y maduro que combina 'on cloud nine' + 'on edge'. Muestra dominio de idiom range para estados emocionales complejos (euforia inicial + ansiedad delayed). Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'came in,', tono descendente en 'on edge'. Contracciones: 'I'd' se contrae si aplica; 'weirdly' es adverbio muy nativo de auto-observacion emocional. Registro: intimo-reflexivo, tipico de conversacion con amigo cercano.
examples: She was over the moon at first, then down in the dumps once reality hit and the pressure began. → arco emocional
I'm in high spirits today, but honestly, I've been on edge all week — hard to explain. → complejidad emocional

questions.prompt: En la fiesta sorpresa, entra tu abuela y ve a toda la familia junta despues de meses.
questions.question: 'Her face lit up when she saw them' means:
options: Her face was literally on fire.
Her face showed sudden joy and brightness.
Her face turned pale from fear.
Her face reddened with anger.
questions.explanation: 'Face lit up' = expresion visible de alegria repentina, casi como si la cara emitiera luz. Muy visual, usado en narrativa emocional: reencuentros, sorpresas positivas, momentos entre padres e hijos. Registro: neutro-literario, comun en storytelling. Colocacion: 'X's face lit up when...' + evento desencadenante. Verbo 'light up' es phrasal verb; en pasado 'lit up' (irregular). Error hispano: no confundir con 'light up' como fumar (contexto lo desambigua).
examples: Her face lit up when she opened the gift — she'd wanted that camera for years. → reaccion visible
His whole face lit up talking about his kids — you could tell they were his world. → orgullo paternal

questions.statement: 'To have a chip on one's shoulder' means to carry resentment or defensiveness from past experiences.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Chip on shoulder' = resentimiento cronico o actitud defensiva, tipicamente originada en experiencias pasadas de haber sido menospreciado. Origen: costumbre americana del siglo XIX en que un hombre desafiante ponia un chip (astilla) en su hombro retando a que se lo quitaran. Muy usado en psychology, HR, y analisis de personajes. Registro: neutro-analitico. Error hispano: traducir literal — hay que usar 'estar resentido' o 'tener complejo'.
examples: He's got a chip on his shoulder about not going to college — brings it up constantly. → resentimiento cronico
She carries a chip on her shoulder from being underestimated early in her career. → analisis empatico

questions.prompt: Vas a subir al escenario a hacer tu primera keynote frente a 500 personas.
questions.question: 'I've got butterflies in my stomach' means:
options: I have literally eaten insects.
I'm feeling nervous and excited at the same time.
I'm suffering from indigestion.
I'm feeling physically ill.
questions.explanation: 'Butterflies in stomach' = mezcla de nervios y emocion pre-evento, sensacion fisica real en el plexo solar. Colocacion tipica: pre-entrevista, primera cita, examen, presentacion, competicion. Registro: neutro-conversacional, muy comun tambien en literatura infantil y juvenil. Diferencia con 'nervous': 'butterflies' implica mezcla positiva de excitement + ansiedad, no solo miedo. Sinonimos: 'butterflies', 'jitters' (mas americano), 'nerves' (mas neutro).
examples: I had butterflies before the interview — 30 seconds before they called my name. → momento pre-clave
She still gets butterflies before every performance, even after 20 years on stage. → nervios cronicos

questions.text: Honestly, I feel like I'm walking on eggshells around him ever since the argument.
questions.explanation: 'Walking on eggshells' = actuar con extrema cautela por miedo a provocar reaccion negativa. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'walking on' con enlazado /ˈwɔːkɪŋɒn/; 'eggshells' con /gʃ/ cluster consonantico, la /g/ tiende a debilitarse. 'Ever since' se enlaza como una unidad /ˌevəˈsɪns/ (la /r/ intrusiva es tipica en el UK). Idiom emocional relacional muy usado; senal clara de relacion tensa (pareja, jefe, familiar). Registro: neutro-conversacional. 'Honestly' como discourse marker anade tono confidencial.
examples: I've been walking on eggshells with my boss lately — she's been unpredictable since the reorg. → tension laboral
Nobody should have to walk on eggshells in their own home — that's not normal. → intervencion emocional seria

questions.prompt: Le explicas a un colega el estado de una amiga que acaba de perder a su madre.
questions.question: 'She was beside herself with grief' means:
options: She was physically standing next to her own body.
She was overwhelmed by intense emotion.
She was completely neutral about it.
She was calm and composed.
questions.explanation: 'Beside oneself' = fuera de si por emocion intensa, incapaz de contenerla. Se combina con 'with' + emocion: 'beside herself with grief/joy/anger/worry'. Registro: formal-literario, mas comun en narrativa escrita que en habla casual. Origen medieval: la idea de que el alma se separaba (staba 'al lado de') del cuerpo bajo emocion extrema. Error hispano: no confundir con 'beside her' (junto a ella, fisico) — 'beside HERSELF' con reflexivo es crucial.
examples: He was beside himself when he heard the news — took him days to speak coherently. → dolor extremo
She was beside herself with worry when the kids didn't come home. → ansiedad paterna aguda

questions.statement: 'To let one's guard down' means to become less defensive and more emotionally open.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Let one's guard down' = bajar las defensas, dejar de protegerse emocionalmente. Metafora de esgrima/boxeo (bajar la guardia). Momento clave de vulnerabilidad: puede ser positivo (intimidad, confianza construida) o riesgoso (permite traicion). Colocacion: 'let MY/HIS/HER guard down' (siempre posesivo). Registro: neutro, comun en therapy talk y narrativa relacional. Error hispano: existe traduccion casi literal ('bajar la guardia') — funciona muy similar en ambos idiomas.
examples: I don't let my guard down easily — trust has to be earned over time with me. → autoconocimiento
Once he let his guard down, we became close friends — but it took years. → construccion de amistad

questions.target: I finally let my guard down and told him how I really felt — it was terrifying, but it took a weight off my shoulders.
questions.explanation: Narrativa emocional madura que combina 'let guard down' + 'take weight off shoulders'. Arco tipico: vulnerabilidad + alivio. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'felt —', tono grave en 'terrifying', tono ascendente y liberador en 'took a weight off'. Contracciones: 'it's' obligatorio. 'Honestly' o 'genuinely' pueden anadirse como discourse markers. Registro: intimo-confesional, tipico de terapia o conversacion con mejor amigo. Muestra dominio de dos idioms emocionales enlazados coherentemente.
examples: Letting my guard down was terrifying at first, but freeing in the end. → arco emocional
Once she opened up, it took a weight off both of us — we'd been dancing around it for months. → alivio mutuo
